html:
The Stoney, or Nakoda, are a Siouan-speaking people of the foothills of the Rocky Mountains in Alberta, Canada. Their language is close to that of the Assiniboine, from whom they split some centuries ago.

In 1492 their ancestors likely lived further east, and they moved west over time, many settling in the foothills and mountain valleys. There they hunted bison, elk and sheep, and were known as fine guides through the mountains. Their neighbours included the Blackfoot, the Tsuut'ina and the Ktunaxa.

Methodist missionaries founded a mission at Morley in 1873. In 1877 the Stoney signed Treaty 7 with Canada, and the Morley reserve west of Calgary became their main home.
